$comment: CDK feature-flag posture. Every flag aws-cdk-lib ships for a service this repo wraps carries a decision here; `node scripts/cdk-flags.mjs check` fails when CDK adds one that does not, and when a package exists with no entry in "modules". Flags for services we do not wrap are out of scope and deliberately absent. Flags CDK declares but removed in v2 are skipped — `check` derives those from the absence of introducedIn.v2, so they are bookkeeping rather than decisions. Statuses: "adopted" (set in packages/examples/cdk.json, with the value), "declined" (a deliberate no), "no-effect" (measured to change nothing — see statusReasons). "recommended" pins what CDK recommended when the decision was made, so a changed recommendation reopens it. The reason is the point of the file: a status without one fails the check.

statusReasons.no-effect: Setting it at its recommended value changes nothing in the assembly `cdk-flags audit` synthesises — 14 example stacks, roughly 20 of the ~50 builder factories, compared on each stack's whole cloud-assembly artifact rather than a chosen subset of its fields. Of those fields only the template, stack tags and stack dependencies vary between examples today; the rest are synthesizer constants. Evidence about what the examples ship, not a claim about every builder and prop, and not about deploy-time or runtime behaviour.

@aws-cdk/aws-apigateway:disableCloudWatc.because: The examples assert on the ApiGateway Account and CloudWatch Role that cleanDeskPolicy tears down; adopting it would delete those resources and the assertions with them. A consumer should adopt it — the role is an account-wide singleton — and #501 made cleanDeskPolicy survive that.

@aws-cdk/aws-ec2:restrictDefaultSecurity.because: VpcBuilder already sets restrictDefaultSecurityGroup on the prop (packages/ec2/src/vpc-defaults.ts), so the guarantee holds without the flag. This is the doctrine the rest of the library follows: a guarantee that depends on the consumer's context is not a guarantee.

@aws-cdk/aws-ec2:uniqueImdsv2TemplateNam.because: Logical-name churn only, on a launch template CDK creates internally. No guarantee at stake, and adopting it replaces the resource in any deployed stack.

@aws-cdk/aws-iam:minimizePolicies.because: Merges IAM statements across 12 example stacks. A policy-size optimisation with no guarantee at stake, and statement merging changes what a reviewer reads in a synthesised policy — which is the point of the consumer-side grants in ADR-0013. Worth adopting on its own, with its own snapshot review.

@aws-cdk/aws-lambda:recognizeLayerVersio.because: Folds a function's layer properties into the hash behind `fn.currentVersion`. Was `no-effect` until an example published a version: `.invokeOnDeploy()` addresses its handler by `currentVersion`, so without this a layer change leaves the version — and therefore the deploy-time invocation — pointing at stale code.

@aws-cdk/aws-lambda:useCdkManagedLogGrou.because: FunctionBuilder already creates the log group explicitly, so the flag is a no-op for builder users — the one stack it changes is CDK's own BucketDeployment Lambda. Kept unset so that stays visible: the guarantee comes from the builder, not the context.

@aws-cdk/aws-s3:publicAccessBlockedByDef.because: The flag fills in any BlockPublicAccess option left undefined. BucketBuilder already sets BLOCK_ALL (packages/s3/src/defaults.ts), so there is nothing left to fill — not because the path is unexercised.

@aws-cdk/aws-s3:serverAccessLogsUseBucke.because: Would be an improvement — without it the access-logs bucket bucket-builder.ts creates carries AccessControl LogDeliveryWrite and ObjectWriter ownership, i.e. ACLs enabled. The builder cannot express that guarantee itself (objectOwnership BUCKET_OWNER_ENFORCED is a synth error while the flag is off), so it needs the decision in issue #502 rather than a manifest entry.

@aws-cdk/core:annotationsInValidationRep.because: Routes every construct annotation into validation-report.json, and scripts/check-validation-report.mjs fails on any violation at any severity — so adopting it turns today's warnings into build failures. Revisit if that checker gains a severity filter.

@aws-cdk/core:defaultCrossStackReference.because: CI deploys and destroys these stacks on every run, so the producer protection "strong" buys is the wrong trade, and a lingering export is a common cause of a teardown that will not finish. See docs/stack-management.md#cross-stack-references.

@aws-cdk/core:enableAdditionalMetadataCo.because: Expands the usage data CDK sends AWS to include L2 property keys, BOOL/ENUM property values and method names. That is a consumer's call, not one the examples should make on their behalf by being the pattern people copy — and it churns the Analytics blob in all 14 stacks. It read `no-effect` until the audit started synthesising with version reporting on: without that there is no AWS::CDK::Metadata resource for it to touch.

@aws-cdk/core:explicitStackTags.because: Stack tagging is exercised heavily here. The flag makes Tags.of() skip aws:cdk:stack, and #498 made StackBuilder.tag() and tags({ system }) apply stack-level tags through a second, stack-scoped aspect so they survive it either way.

@aws-cdk/core:validateAgainstDefaultRule.because: Left unset by #339. Every rule the ruleset currently raises against the examples is warning severity, and check-validation-report.mjs already fails on those, so adopting it changes nothing today while adding a second gate that can disagree with the first.

@aws-cdk/custom-resources:logApiResponse.because: CDK recommends false, which is also the unconfigured behaviour, so adopting it changes nothing — the flag only bites when set true, where it adds an Update event that breaks callers depending on response data. AwsCustomResourceBuilder never sets logApiResponseData, so the caller keeps that choice.

@aws-cdk/customresources:installLatestAw.because: CDK recommends false, which is also the unconfigured behaviour, so adopting it changes nothing — it is a structural no-op rather than an unmeasured one.
